scope: The existing Saturday Spin P0 release plus the Not Done Yet application workflow, including the new staged post-submission review and approved next-step presentation, personal actions, delivery APIs, admin follow-up views, analytics privacy controls and scheduled retries.

sections.readerQuestion: Can readers rely on the corrected newsletter reach and stable Core Training Guide delivery introduced on main?
sections.usefulAnswer: The inherited main revision retains the corrected 23,000-reader proof, attribution handling and verified PDF route.
sections.evidence: Main already carried exact-revision publication evidence for these surfaces before the Not Done Yet branch was reconciled.
sections.editorialDecision: Preserve the reviewed main-branch work without reopening or weakening its claims.

sections.location: /apply form, confirmation, /apply/next review transition and after-application FAQ
sections.readerQuestion: What happens when I submit my coaching application?
sections.usefulAnswer: With the feature enabled, a saved Not Done Yet application moves through four short review messages before confirming approval and offering the join and Sarah paths; Inner Circle retains its existing process.
sections.evidence: Anthony requested the immediate two-option flow on 8 September 2026 and the staged post-submission review on 9 September 2026. The server flag gates the workflow and visible form copy.
sections.editorialDecision: Present the deterministic result after a deliberate eight-second transition, avoid implying a separate human decision, and preserve existing copy when the feature is disabled.

sections.location: /apply/next approval, join, onboarding and questions sections
sections.readerQuestion: How do I join, or ask about the coaching before paying?
sections.usefulAnswer: Approved applicants can start a seven-day risk-free trial before the stated monthly plan, learn that the team will arrange onboarding inside Skool, or send Sarah a question linked to their application.
sections.evidence: The live Skool plan was checked at seven days free followed by $195 USD per month plus applicable taxes. Anthony supplied the approval, onboarding and Sarah hold-or-question instructions.
sections.editorialDecision: Keep the two actions and two numbered steps explicit; describe availability without a countdown, quantity or unsupported scarcity claim.

sections.location: Application API, database outbox, Beehiiv adapter, cron and Anthony notification sender
sections.readerQuestion: Will applications and questions survive a delivery problem?
sections.usefulAnswer: The application and email job commit together; questions save before notification; known failures retry within bounds while uncertain enrollments stop for inspection.
sections.evidence: One hundred and sixteen focused tests cover deduplication, opt-outs, marker ordering, accepted-journey confirmation, saved questions, Anthony routing and retry boundaries; the production table, draft transactions and live provider configuration were also verified.
sections.editorialDecision: Use precise delivery states, preserve opt-outs and payment state, and never equate checkout interest with payment.

sections.readerQuestion: Can staff see who needs a reply without exposing a personal action token?
sections.usefulAnswer: Authenticated staff can see the dedicated Sarah Review column, delivery and question status, while analytics and referrer leakage are suppressed on the personal next-step page.
sections.evidence: The implementation uses existing admin authentication, assigns question records to Sarah, alerts Anthony, and keeps personal tokens in URL fragments and POST bodies rather than query strings.
sections.editorialDecision: Expose useful operational states only to staff and scope analytics suppression to the personal action surface.

claimsAndSources: The workflow and inbox routing come from Anthony's 8 September 2026 instructions; the staged review, approval, onboarding and Sarah hold-or-question language come from his 9 September 2026 brief. The seven-day trial and $195 USD monthly price were checked on the live Skool plan; Sarah's direct address and ownership are confirmed in repository configuration. Existing main-branch audience and PDF claims remain unchanged.
examplesAndReasoning: The suitability result is determined by the existing goal, time and injury/comeback routing rule before this page loads. The four-message transition presents that completed application review; it is not described as a medical or human assessment. No training prescription or member result is invented.
voiceAndCuts: The approved state uses the requested congratulatory tone, two numbered setup steps and a calm Sarah alternative. The transition gives each of the four review messages two seconds, creating a deliberate pause without a countdown, queue-position or limited-place claim.
desktopReview: The exact source was rendered at 1432 by 900 CSS pixels for the staged review and approved personal next-step page. All four messages appeared at roughly two-second intervals before approval, the browser reported no warnings and the page had no horizontal overflow.
mobileReview: The exact source was rendered in a 390 by 844 CSS pixel browser viewport for the staged review and approved personal next-step page. The loader card, headings, price, buttons and sections wrapped correctly; the eight-second transition completed and there was no horizontal overflow.
productAndOfferAccuracy: The live Skool offer showed a seven-day free trial followed by $195 USD per month plus applicable taxes. The dedicated Beehiiv automation is live with personalised destinations and the publication reply-to remains Anthony; website questions persist in Sarah Review and send Anthony an operational alert.
